title: Dark mode for an existing site
when: The user wants an existing site or app to get a dark version that follows the system setting, with every component readable in it.
prompt:
Goal: Every hard coded color replaced by semantic tokens, a tuned dark palette applied through prefers-color-scheme, and no component left unreadable.
Steps:
1. Audit the CSS for literal colors, including shadows, borders, gradients and inline SVG fills.
2. Map them to semantic tokens on :root: --bg, --surface, --surface-raised, --text, --muted, --accent, --border, --shadow; replace every literal.
3. Write dark values inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { ... } }, plus a [data-theme="dark"] copy if a manual switch exists.
4. Tune the dark palette: base #121212 to #1e1e1e, raised surfaces lighter instead of shadows, text near #e8e8e8, softer accents.
5. Fix media: SVG icons use currentColor, logos get a dark variant, photos get a slight brightness reduction, charts get a dark set.
6. Set color-scheme: light dark on :root so native controls and scrollbars follow.
Quality bar:
- Text pairs reach 4.5 to 1 in the dark palette too.
- Elevation reads through surface lightness.
- No component keeps a light background by accident.
Pitfalls:
- A global invert filter.
- Literal colors left inside components and pseudo elements.
- Pure white text on pure black that glares.
Verify:
- [ ] A prefers-color-scheme dark rule exists.
- [ ] No literal colors remain outside the token blocks.
- [ ] Dark text pairs pass contrast.
- [ ] Any saved theme choice reads storage safely.
Output: style.css with the token blocks and components switched to tokens, and a short list of the color mappings.

examples.input: adicione modo escuro no meu site
examples.output: 42 literal colors mapped to 9 tokens, dark palette via prefers-color-scheme, SVG icons on currentColor
